name: The editor reports real frame times and has a vsync toggle
body:
# Real frame times in the editor

The status bar always shows 60 fps on the course world, even with LANTERN_VSYNC=0, while the game reports 185-234 fps.

Cause (found by reading the code): the editor window's SDL renderer is hard-coded to vsync (`SdlWindow.Open` in penumbra-ui-engine calls `SDL_SetRenderVSync(renderer, 1)`) and the editor redraws every frame, so each frame waits for the display. LANTERN_VSYNC only reaches the off-screen GPU renderer, which has no swapchain. The fps figure is the time between viewport renders, so it measured a vsync-paced loop.

Plan: `SdlWindow.SetVerticalSync`; the editor honours LANTERN_VSYNC at start and has a VSync toggle in the Graphics tab; the status bar shows wall-clock frame time (average and worst over the last 120 frames), fps from it, the GPU render time and whether vsync is on. The editor has no idle mode (it redraws continuously), so there is no redraw toggle.

Open question: none; decision recorded as D-078.
